title: Naming Cartographer, then rebuilding it properly
goal: Put a fuzzy idea into words (a tool that records vibecoding sessions and maps how you build), then make it real: a concept doc and a working /wrap prototype, then a rebuild that is agent-agnostic, language-aware and configurable.
outcome: Named it Cartographer; set solo + teams tiers with the end-of-project replay as the core moment; shipped a v1 prototype in 6 minutes of build time; then rebuilt it as a package with three agent adapters, a prompt-pragmatics layer, aptitude-based config, git-repo projects with branches, auto-wrap hooks, tests and skills.

phases.name: Articulate
phases.summary: Brain-dump turned into a framing and pitch

phases.name: Decide
phases.summary: Four product calls in one message, after a 19-minute pause

phases.name: Prototype v1
phases.summary: Transcript parser, replay page, two skills, concept doc, in about 6 minutes of build

phases.name: Rebuild
phases.summary: Agent-agnostic package with adapters, pragmatics, config, hooks and tests

steps.title: Brain-dump the workflow recorder idea
steps.detail: Described a connector that records AI coding sessions and builds a profile and mind map over time. Descriptive mode, no anchors, no done-condition: a pure articulation request.
steps.prompt: OKAY. i have an app idea, designed for the future of vibecoding. It's a connector to your AI agent that records and analyzes your workflow in the CLI or agent itself… im having trouble aritculating this. help me.

steps.title: Frame: flight recorder for vibecoding
steps.detail: Git records what changed, chat logs record everything, nothing records how you thought. That gap became the product's one-line thesis.

steps.title: Pitch replay as a next-project hook
steps.detail: The agent proposed the magic moment was surfacing an old playbook when a new project starts. The user reframed it: the moment is the end-of-project replay.

steps.title: Ask: who is it for, private or social?
steps.detail: Three sharpening questions closed the first reply. All three were answered in the next prompt.

steps.title: Answer with four decisions at once
steps.detail: After 19 minutes away: two editions, social optional, killer moment defined, name chosen, and two deliverables requested in one message.
steps.prompt: I want to make two versions- solo and teams. You have the option to make it social- we'd need a database backend for that. What do you mean by killer moment? The killer moment is the replay- when you get to see your workflow at the end of the project version. I want a concept doc AND a /wrap protoype. Cartographer is a good name.

steps.title: Killer moment = end-of-project replay
steps.detail: Reuse comes after the replay, not instead of it. This ordered the whole build: replay page first, profile later.

steps.title: Name it Cartographer
steps.detail: Picked from the shortlist; it fits the map framing and gave the doc and the replay page a shared identity.

steps.title: Inspect Claude Code's transcript format
steps.detail: Sessions are JSONL under ~/.claude/projects with prompts, replies, tool calls, gitBranch and timestamps. Capture needs no new infrastructure.

steps.title: digest.py, render.py, /wrap, /replay
steps.detail: A transcript compressor, an animated replay page, and two skills, written and tested on this very session in under four minutes.

steps.title: Preview the replay from file://
steps.detail: The browser pane refused the file URL. A one-line static-server config fixed it; not a code bug, a tooling constraint.

steps.title: Serve the demo over localhost
steps.detail: Added .claude/launch.json with a python http.server entry; playback and the playbook section then verified in the browser.

steps.title: Concept doc with survey-map identity
steps.detail: Published the doc as an artifact and retrofitted its palette onto the replay page so doc and product read as one thing.

steps.title: Rebuild: agent-agnostic, language-aware, configurable
steps.detail: After a 56-minute pause, a large-scope prompt with one constraint and no done-condition: adapters for the three most popular agents, prompt pragmatics per language, retrospective maps, manual/auto wrap, aptitude-based feedback, projects as git repos with branches, and a pricing sketch. The agent chose the architecture.
steps.prompt: Rebuild this using Fable. I want the code written advanced enough to capture nuances regardless of the model used to do the coding. Basically, agent agnostic for creating the map but should be built for the three most popular coding agents…

steps.title: Check Python version and agent data on disk
steps.detail: Python 3.9.6 (no match/tomllib) and only Claude Code data present. Set two constraints: write to 3.9, and cover Codex and Cursor with synthetic fixtures.

steps.title: Restart at higher effort
steps.detail: The user raised the effort level and asked for a restart. The folder had already been reset, so the rebuild proceeded from a clean layout.
steps.prompt: restart with the effort level changed

steps.title: Common event model, one adapter per agent
steps.detail: Every adapter emits prompt/reply/tool/error/branch/note events; digest, brief and recap only see that model. Adding an agent is one file.

steps.title: Brief file makes mapping agent-agnostic
steps.detail: Instead of a Claude-only skill, `cartographer wrap` writes a Markdown brief any agent can follow (rules, reader profile, language notes, timeline). Claude Code, Codex and Cursor all consume the same file.

steps.title: lang.py: detection + prompt pragmatics
steps.detail: Language/framework detection from files, pasted code and mentions; per-prompt reading (act, anchoring, specificity, vagueness, delegation, scope) with coaching signals; standing notes per language as priors.

steps.title: Smoke test on the live session
steps.detail: Brief generated end to end. Two fixes from reading it: Claude Code's `HEAD` branch means no repo, and prompt #3 was misread as `config` because of generic words like `version`.

steps.title: Stem-tolerant intent matching
steps.detail: One test failed: 'make it look nicer… you decide the colors' scored as build. Matching now tolerates inflections and ties break away from build. 12/12 tests pass.

steps.title: Dogfood: wrap this session with the rebuild
steps.detail: This recap was written by following the generated brief and saved with `cartographer save`.

reusable_prompts.prompt: I have an idea for <thing>. I'm having trouble articulating it. Help me.
reusable_prompts.why: Returns a framing, a structure, pitch variants and the questions that sharpen the idea.

reusable_prompts.prompt: Rebuild <thing> so that it is <property 1>, <property 2>, <property 3>. It must support <A>, <B>, <C>. A <unit of work> is <definition>.
reusable_prompts.why: Batching every requirement into one message let the agent design the architecture once instead of iterating; the cost is that the agent picks the architecture.

patterns: Starts from a messy brain-dump and lets the agent find the words, then corrects the framing.
Steps away to think between framing and deciding (19 min, then 56 min) rather than iterating in chat; comes back with batched decisions.
Makes product decisions fast once shown concrete options: four calls in one message.
Wants both the story (concept doc) and the thing (prototype) at once.
Raises scope sharply after seeing a first version work, and sets quality constraints ('advanced enough to capture nuances') without done-conditions.

time_sinks.what: Thinking pause between pitch and decisions (productive)
Pause between v1 delivery and the rebuild request
Writing the rebuild: adapters, lang, digest, brief, render, hooks, cli, tests

coaching.observation: The rebuild prompt listed eight capabilities but no done-condition, so 'done' was whatever the agent decided to ship.
coaching.suggestion: Add one acceptance line per capability you care most about; it becomes the test list.
coaching.rewrite: Rebuild this as an agent-agnostic package. Done means: (1) `cartographer wrap` works on a Claude Code, Codex and Cursor session, (2) the brief includes a per-prompt reading and language notes, (3) config switches voice and feedback by aptitude, (4) projects are git repos with branches shown in the replay, (5) tests pass on Python 3.9.

coaching.observation: Batching four decisions after a pause worked well: the agent could start building immediately.
coaching.suggestion: Keep doing this; when you batch, also say which item matters most so the agent can order the work.

coaching.observation: The Codex and Cursor adapters are written from format knowledge and synthetic fixtures, not real data.
coaching.suggestion: Before relying on them, run `cartographer sessions --agent codex` on a machine with Codex history and fix whatever the adapter misses; the formats shift between releases.

next_steps: Move the checkout into the new repo and run `./bin/cartographer install --agent all`.
Validate the Codex and Cursor adapters against real history.
Design the sync service and the team workspace schema for the paid tiers.
Try `cartographer backfill` on an older repo to test retrospective maps.
